environment.description: Same Django REST API deployed on EC2 behind an Application Load Balancer. The ALB has an associated AWS WAFv2 Web ACL (arn:aws:wafv2:us-east-1:123456789012:regional/webacl/doc-api-protection/a1b2c3d4) with the following rule groups in priority order: (1) AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet with SizeRestrictions_BODY rule action override to COUNT, (2) a custom rule 'block-pickle-signatures' with priority 1 that inspects request Body with a RegexPatternSet matching byte sequences '\x80\x0[2-5]' (pickle protocol headers) and base64-encoded variants of pickle opcodes including 'gASV', 'KRVU', 'jASV' with action BLOCK, (3) AWS-AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet in default BLOCK mode which includes rules for deserialization payloads. The Web ACL default action is ALLOW. CloudWatch metrics confirm the custom rule fires on test payloads. Note: the SizeRestrictions override to COUNT means large payloads are still permitted through, only the content-pattern rules provide protection.

config.infrastructure: AWS EC2 t3.medium, ALB with WAFv2 Web ACL associated
config.network: VPC with public subnet, ALB listener on port 443 forwarding to target group on port 8000
